title: non-GMO & USDA Organic Explained | Ask Organic Valley
summary: Dairy co-op explainer that USDA organic always means non-GMO but non-GMO labelling does not mean organic, and that organic rules bar GMO feed, antibiotics and synthetic hormones.

assertions.quote: product with the non-GMO label is not necessarily certified organic.

verdicts.note: Non-GMO verification covers only genetic engineering, not pesticides, fertilisers or livestock practices.

Avoiding excluded (genetic engineering) methods is only one of seven prohibitions in 7 CFR 205.105, beside synthetic substances, irradiation and sewage sludge, and organic also requires certification (205.100), so non-GMO alone does not meet the organic standard.

assertions.quote: USDA certified organic always means non-GMO
free of antibiotics, toxic pesticides, synthetic hormones and GMOs.
